long_biography.plain_text:
Buying a New York Stock Exchange seat gave Carl Icahn the platform for an independent securities firm. His uncle and client Elliot Schnall lent most of the purchase price, after Icahn had learned options trading and arbitrage on Wall Street. He later shifted from price discrepancies to substantial corporate stakes, turning concentrated positions into leverage over management and boards.

The analytical habits behind that strategy had earlier drawn him to philosophy at Princeton, where his senior thesis won an award. Icahn eventually directed part of his fortune toward medical research. His support for Mount Sinai led the institution to rename its medical school for him and expand research in genomics and translational medicine.
